Header: Aphis craccivora ( syn. Aphis atronitens ) groundnut aphid in English, inda shamufilimwa in Zambian Bemba language

Prevention: Grow aphid repellent plant (marigold and onion) as border/ barrier around groundnut
Conserve natural enemies by avoiding broad spectrum insecticides and keeping flowering weeds
Apply poultry manure (850kg/ha) to ensure high plant vigour.
This kind of fertiliser does not attract aphids as nitrogen fertilizers do
Use planting space of 45cm between rows and 20cm between plants leading to 89000 plant per hectare (runner type)
Burn dried cow dung and shrub leaves to make smoke early mornings or late evening to repel aphids
Monitoring: Monitor groundnuts from germination up to maturity once a week
Look for yellowing leaves, honeydew, and stunted growth
Observe underside of the leaves for grey-black or green aphids (often in colonies)
Aphids are tiny 1 to 2 mm pear-shaped soft insects.
You may also see ants associated with aphids.
When you see 2 to 3 plants of 20 to 30 plants having some aphids, you may consider green control.
When you see 4 to 10 out of 20-30 plants having at least 2 aphid colonies you may consider chemical control
It is considered to too late to act if you have 80-100% plants affected by aphids
Action may also not be needed late in the season.
Direct Control: Release biocontrol agents e.g. ladybirds, parasitic wasps, laceways, obtained at research stations.

Early in the aphid infestation apply botanical mixture containing chilli or garlic (chop 10 garlic cloves, add 5 to 6 plastic-bottle lids or 4-5 tablespoons of mineral oil or liquid paraffin, add 1litre or 4 cups warm water) spray 5 cup mixture to 25cup of water
Spray soapy water (8ml/16l water) on the area affected during early morning /late evening so that the spray does not dry quickly
Spray with neem-based products and follow instruction on the label e.g. 1-part azatrol with 1-part water.
Spray into groundnut canopies in the late afternoons when weather is calm.
Spray in 7-10 days intervals if threshold reached.
